newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's zinc firm Iscaycruz awaits tailings permit.
newsitem.headline: Peru's zinc firm Iscaycruz awaits tailings permit.

text.p: Operations at Peru's largest zinc miner Iscaycruz S.A. continue partially halted while it waits for the government to provide it with a permit for a tailings dumping site, a company source said Wednesday.
The government ordered the miner to halt part of its operations last week because the company did not have the right paperwork, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
The order has not affected production, according to the company, which did not specify which area of operations was affected.
"It is purely a procedural problem. There is no problem with production nor with the environment," the company source said.

But industry sources explained that because the company does not have as much space as it wants to dump its tailings, in the short-term at least Iscaycruz would have to reduce output to stop producing so much waste.
"If you have not got a garbage can, you cannot just keep on producing garbage," one industry source said.

Iscaycruz, which has already presented the government with all the appropriate paperwork for the permit, was due to make a public presentation November 10 to explain why it needs the tailings site, the company source said.
In July, Iscaycruz, which is controlled by Switzerland's Glencore Group, started production of zinc concentrates at its 125,000 tonne capacity mine.

The Iscaycruz mine - situated more than 4,500 meters (15,000 feet) above sea level in the Andean province of Oyon 100 miles (160 km) northeast of Lima - also has a capacity to produce around 9,000 tonnes annually of lead concentrates.

Iscaycruz expects to exploit for at least seven years its proven and probable mineral reserves of 2.7 million tonnes, which have one of the highest zinc grades in the world at 21.4 percent. The reserves' lead grade is 2.2 percent.
